title: Creative Entrepreneurship
overview: Creative entrepreneurship combines opportunity recognition, innovative thinking, customer understanding, experimentation, and disciplined business development. Successful entrepreneurial ideas are not defined only by originality; they must solve meaningful problems, create value for a clearly identified customer or beneficiary, and be developed into models that can be tested, improved, and sustained.

This course takes participants through the entrepreneurial journey from identifying opportunities and generating ideas to defining value propositions, understanding customers, designing business models, testing assumptions, developing minimum viable solutions, considering financial viability, building a market-entry approach, and presenting a convincing entrepreneurial concept.

The program emphasizes practical application. Participants will work individually and in teams on an entrepreneurial challenge, using creativity tools, customer-discovery methods, business-model thinking, prototyping, validation, basic financial analysis, branding, marketing, pitching, and implementation planning to transform an initial idea into a structured business concept.
audience: Aspiring entrepreneurs, startup founders, professionals considering new ventures, innovation teams, business-development personnel, SME owners, project leaders, creative professionals, and employees responsible for developing new products, services, business models, or entrepreneurial initiatives.
methodology: The course uses a highly practical methodology combining short presentations, entrepreneurial case studies, opportunity-discovery exercises, creativity workshops, customer-persona development, value-proposition activities, business-model design, competitor analysis, prototyping, validation exercises, financial-planning activities, marketing and branding workshops, pitching practice, peer feedback, and a final venture-development presentation. Participants progressively develop one entrepreneurial concept throughout the program.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain the entrepreneurial process from opportunity identification to business launch and development.
Identify problems, unmet needs, trends, and changes that can create entrepreneurial opportunities.
Apply structured creativity techniques to generate and improve business ideas.
Define target customers and develop evidence-based understanding of their needs and behavior.
Create a clear value proposition that explains why customers should choose the proposed solution.
Design a practical business model covering customers, channels, relationships, activities, resources, partners, revenues, and costs.
Assess market conditions, alternatives, competitors, and sources of differentiation.
Identify critical business assumptions and test them through customer discovery, prototypes, and minimum viable solutions.
Estimate basic startup costs, pricing considerations, revenues, and financial viability.
Develop an initial branding, marketing, and market-entry approach.
Prepare and deliver a persuasive entrepreneurial pitch.
Create an actionable roadmap for developing the venture after the course.
